prompt: Which modules listen for the 'shift.claimed' event? For each one, name the file and the function that registers the listener. Do not change any file.
Fix the typo "excceded" in the capacity error message in src/booking.js.

toCsv in src/reports.js joins fields with commas as they are, so a shift titled "Dock, north" or a location with a double quote or a line break corrupts the CSV. Make toCsv quote a field (header labels included) when it contains a comma, a double quote, a CR or an LF, doubling any double quote inside, as RFC 4180 does. Fields that need no quoting stay as they are, and keep the current line separator. Add tests.

Booking breaks under load in production: a shift sometimes ends up with more workers than its capacity, or the same worker twice, and now and then a worker who got a successful claim is missing from the shift afterwards. The tests never show it. Find the cause and fix it, so that every rule src/booking.js enforces still holds, and no successful change to a shift is lost, when requests run concurrently. Requests that do not conflict must still succeed, and must not wait for each other. Add a test that reproduces the problem.
Rename sumMinutes to totalMinutes in src/payroll.js and everywhere it is used, tests included.

Add date filters to listShifts in src/shifts.js and to GET /shifts: optional `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM-DD, both inclusive) keep only the shifts whose start falls in that range, as a calendar date in the shift's own time zone. A malformed or impossible date is a ValidationError (400 over HTTP). Add tests.

Security report: GET /shifts/:id/attachments/:name serves files from outside the attachments folder, for example /shifts/shf_1/attachments/..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd. Fix readAttachment in src/attachments.js so that it, and so the endpoint, only ever returns a file that saveAttachment stored for that shift. For anything else it must throw a NotFoundError (404 over HTTP), never another error. Add a test for the report.
Tokens expire too fast for the night crew. Make the default token lifetime 30 minutes instead of 15.

Offboarding, three changes. (1) Rename the event 'user.deactivated' to 'user.offboarded' everywhere. (2) deactivateUser must also take the user off every shift that has not started yet (start > now()), emitting 'shift.released' with { shiftId, userId } for each one; shifts that already started keep them, and it still returns the user. (3) A deactivated user's tokens must stop working at once: every route that needs a token answers 401 when the token's user is deactivated or does not exist, including tokens issued before the deactivation. Add tests for each change.

Add shift cancellation. cancelShift(shiftId, { reason }) in src/shifts.js, exported from src/index.js, sets the shift's status to 'cancelled' and emits 'shift.cancelled' with { shiftId, reason, assignees }, where assignees are the workers who were on it. A cancelled shift cannot be claimed (ConflictError), and listShifts({ status: 'cancelled' }) finds it. Add POST /shifts/:id/cancel for managers only, with the reason in the body. Add tests.

Three changes to recurring shifts. (1) A series may now cover up to 92 days instead of 62. (2) createRecurring takes an optional `skip` list of YYYY-MM-DD dates to leave out; a malformed or impossible date in it is a ValidationError, and dates outside from..to are ignored. (3) Wall-clock times around DST changes come out wrong in some zones. Make localToInstant in src/time.js, and so createRecurring, follow one rule in every zone: a time inside a spring-forward gap moves forward by the length of the gap (02:30 on the night New York jumps from 02:00 to 03:00 becomes 03:30 EDT), and a time that happens twice when the clocks fall back means its first occurrence. Add tests.

Every module in src/ keeps its state at module level, so one process can only run one shiftboard. We need several tenants in one process. Add createApp(options) to src/index.js: it returns an object with the same functions as the top-level exports of src/index.js (all of them except createApp itself), and two apps must share no state at all: data, ids, caches, event listeners, configuration, clock, audit log, and outgoing messages. options takes the same keys as configure(). Every existing top-level export must keep working exactly as it does today; they can be backed by a default app. Keep the tests passing and add tests for the isolation.
